title: Resume
text:
Sustainability Analyst (Data Management Lead) · The Resource Group (Ascension) · Remote
January 2025 – Present

Lead data management for Ascension’s sustainability program across more than 75 hospitals and over 400 sites.
Reduced proxy data in the carbon emissions inventory by 83% from baseline, replacing estimates with activity data to improve the accuracy of emissions tracking:

Built a Python matching process that linked about 7,000 utility accounts to their properties using addresses, account numbers, ZIP codes, meter IDs and custom string-matching rules.
Sourced activity data for mobile fleet operations, and for district steam and chilled water directly from the provider.

Calculate Scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas emissions, capturing 12 of 15 Scope 3 categories: every category relevant to hospital operations.
Forecast carbon emissions with time series models and presented the results to leadership to inform planning for a power purchase agreement (PPA).
Built a Tableau waste dashboard used by Environment of Care committees at 40+ sites of care, tracking year-over-year change in recycling, pounds of regulated medical waste per patient day, and recycling as a share of solid waste to drive friendly competition between sites.
Automated monthly data validation with Python and BigQuery scheduled queries, including outlier flagging, emails to data owners, and syncing data between Google Sheets and BigQuery. This saves about 10 hours of manual work a month.

Tools: Python, R, SQL, BigQuery, Tableau, Power BI, Excel, Google Workspace

title: Ellie Wilser
text:
I’m a sustainability analyst working where healthcare sustainability meets data science. At The Resource Group, an Ascension subsidiary, I lead data management for Ascension’s sustainability program. I calculate Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, build dashboards that help sites track their progress, and automate the review and auditing work behind our reporting.
I’m passionate about sustainability, and I believe good data is what turns sustainability goals into measurable progress. My favorite work is finding the slow, manual process everyone has learned to live with, and rebuilding it so it’s faster, more accurate, and easier to trust.

title: Ellie Wilser
text:
What I’m exploring
In my M.S. in Data Science at CUNY School of Professional Studies, I’m focused on physics-informed machine learning: models that combine the physical laws behind a system with real-world data, so they stay reliable even when data is limited. These models are a natural fit for complex systems like buildings, where both the physics and the data matter.
I’m especially interested in using them to build digital twins, virtual copies of real buildings and systems. A digital twin lets you test a sustainability project before spending money on it. Projects I’d like to model include:

HVAC upgrades and control strategies, such as scheduling and setpoint changes
Building envelope improvements, like insulation, windows and roofing
Solar and battery storage sizing
Energy demand forecasting and load shifting to lower peak usage and emissions
Central plant optimization, such as chillers, boilers and water use

Healthcare facilities are among the most energy-intensive buildings, and they run 24/7. That makes them a high-impact place to get these decisions right.
